cohort: 50 pregnant women with heart disease (25 with corrected heart disease and 25 with non-corrected heart disease) at a tertiary care institute in Kolkata, West Bengal, India.
finding: Pregnant women with non-corrected heart disease are more likely to experience severe cardiac complications, require intensive care unit admission, preterm birth, and deliver low birth weight babies compared to those with corrected heart disease.
mod_finding: Caesarean section rates were similar between the corrected (30%) and non-corrected (34%) heart disease groups.
birth_weight: Low birth weight was more common in the non-corrected group (p<0.05)
